column3: Zetetic. SQLCipher Community Edition License. zetetic.net/sqlcipher/license, accessed 2026-04-25.
column4: SQLCipher CE is BSD-3-clause-style and requires reproducing copyright/attribution in user-accessible UI (about/license screen) and documentation; permits OSS and commercial redistribution but adds a compliance surface.
column6: Authoritative primary source. Drove decision against SQLCipher as primary path.

column4: SQLCipher overhead 5-15% read/write per Zetetic's own benchmarks; default 4 KB page + per-page HMAC.

column3: Turso. Fully Open Source Encryption for SQLite. turso.tech/blog/fully-open-source-encryption-for-sqlite-b3858225, accessed 2026-04-25.
column4: libSQL ships fully OSS page-level encryption with SQLCipher-compatible cipher and AES-256 wxSQLite3 cipher; WAL and bottomless backups also encrypted.
column6: Authoritative primary source for D1. Apache-2.0/MIT.

column6: Confirms operator-facing API surface for D1.

column3: oven-sh / bun. Issue #25964 — Windows NTFS SQLite WAL close() leaves DB locked. github.com/oven-sh/bun/issues/25964, accessed 2026-04-25.
column4: Pre-3.51 SQLite leaves the main .db file locked on Windows NTFS after close() in multi-process WAL access; fixed in SQLite 3.51.0.
column6: Concrete production-bug evidence driving D5 (≥3.51 floor).

column3: SQLite. Write-Ahead Logging documentation. sqlite.org/wal.html, accessed 2026-04-25.
column4: Authoritative WAL mode semantics; shared-memory wal-index requirement; multi-reader / single-writer concurrency model.

column3: SQLite. How to corrupt your SQLite database. sqlite.org/howtocorrupt.html, accessed 2026-04-25.
column4: WAL is unsafe on networked filesystems (NFS SMB CIFS); locking primitives are buggy; shared-memory wal-index cannot be coordinated across hosts.
column6: Authoritative basis for D6 (refuse non-local mounts).
